Definition: properly, to boil up, i.e. (figuratively) to be peevish or angry
BiblicalUsage: Za'aph as a verb means to boil up, to grow peevish and angry. In Genesis 40:6 Joseph finds Pharaoh's officers sad and downcast in prison, and in 2 Chronicles 26:19 Uzziah grows wroth with the priests and leprosy rises in his forehead while he is still angry. Proverbs 19:3 puts it bluntly: "The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the LORD." In Daniel 1:10 the prince of the eunuchs fears the king's displeasure over the young men's faces.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word catches anger at its smallest and most human, in a sad face, a fretting heart, a king's wounded pride. I hold that Uzziah's leprosy in 2 Chronicles 26:19 is the picture of what anger does when it meets God's holiness, and that fretting against the Lord, as Proverbs 19:3 says, is foolishness that perverts my own way. My position is that za'aph should make me hand my anger to God before it boils over.
